claims.text: A 2–5 μm Hf interlayer should be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating.
Approximately 300°C subcritical water represents the normal-operation boundary.
Steam exposure up to approximately 1200°C for about 10 minutes represents an accident-relevant boundary.
The Hf interlayer will react or interdiffuse with the zirconium substrate.
Hf–Zr interaction will form a localized Hf–Zr alloy transition layer.
The resulting Hf–Zr transition layer will be stable under the proposed exposure conditions.
The Hf–Zr transition layer will act as a diffusion barrier that blocks further Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Direct elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion compromises elemental Cr coating integrity.
The Hf-containing barrier will limit migration of zirconium into the Cr coating.
Limiting zirconium migration will minimize degradation of the protective chromium layer.
The Hf interlayer will maintain the coating's corrosion resistance in normal subcritical-water environments.
Relative to Cr deposited directly on zirconium alloy, the Hf-interlayer system will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the unmodified coating, the Hf-interlayer system will have improved coating adhesion.
Relative to the unmodified coating, the Hf-interlayer system will have a lower incidence of premature failure during high-temperature steam exposure.
The Hf-interlayer system will retain excellent corrosion protection during normal subcritical-water exposure.
An elemental Cr coating deposited directly on zirconium alloy is susceptible to premature failure caused by elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The long-term stability of the Hf interlayer under irradiation and cyclic thermal stress is uncertain.
The Hf interlayer's chemical interaction with coolant chemistry over service lifetimes is uncertain.
